name: Towns under the Towns Improvement Act 1959
description: Antrim, the last town under the Towns Improvement (Ireland) Act 1854 in Northern Ireland, after the Aughnacloy and Gilford commissioners were dissolved in 1959, until 31 Mar 1962. The edition is dated by the Belfast Gazette notice of 29 May 1959; the orders' operative date has not been seen. Town commissioners under the 1854 Act levied a limited rate and carried out minor works; for public health each town stayed under its rural district council (1937 Census General Report). Each town is drawn from the DED that matches its legal boundary: Antrim Urban, Aughnacloy Urban, Downpatrick Urban and Whitehead Urban, and Gilford as reconstituted in 1923 (Gilford Town is exactly the Gilford DED in the 1926 and 1951 censuses); Kilkeel is the townlands of Kilkeel and Magheramurphy, which the 1934 boundary order names. The drawn areas agree with the printed town areas within 2.4% (Aughnacloy +0.2%, Whitehead +0.8%, Gilford -2.1%, Antrim -2.3%). No order altering any town's limits has been found in the Belfast Gazette, 1922-1962.

references.note: 25 Dec 1936. Recites that the town of Kilkeel comprised Kilkeel North and Kilkeel South DEDs and part of Kilkeel East DED, and the order of 21 Jul 1936 making it an urban district from 1 Apr 1937.

references.note: 13 Jun 1924. Ministry order separating the town of Downpatrick (a town having commissioners under the 1854 Act) from Downpatrick Rural District as an urban sanitary district from 1 Apr 1925.

references.note: 29 May 1959. Notices of the Local Government (Dissolution of Commissioners) (Aughnacloy) and (Gilford) Orders (NI) 1959, S.R. & O. 1959 Nos. 50 and 51, dissolving the commissioners and transferring their functions.

references.note: 6 Apr 1962. Notice of the Local Government (Dissolution of Commissioners) (Antrim) Order (NI) 1962, S.R. & O. 1962 No. 50, transferring the commissioners' functions to Antrim Rural District Council; the 1961 and 1966 censuses date this 1 Apr 1962.
